Subject: Request: 36-month rate commitment & renewal protection (FintechCo)

Team —

Quick background: FintechCo (Tom Briggs) is ready to commit to a three-year contract for our Enterprise plan — target start date 2026-07-01. They asked for a fixed per-token rate for 36 months, an uplift cap on any annual increase, and a renewal protection clause that restricts price increases at renewal unless agreed 12 months in advance. ACV is $4.2M year 1 (consumption + committed).

Proposed commercial asks from the AE/procurement:
- 36-month fixed per-token rate (price lock)
- Annual uplift cap: 5% (absolute max year-over-year)
- Renewal protection: if Redwood raises list prices >5% at renewal, customer receives the lesser of prior-year rate or a one-time credit to offset impact, and we commit to a 12-month notice window for material pricing changes
- One-time onboarding discount: 20% off first-year committed spend to meet procurement thresholds

Why escalate: the combined effect (3-year lock + 20% upfront + uplift cap) exceeds standard deal desk tolerances. Finance and Legal will need to confirm revenue recognition and risk. Procurement has requested exec signoff by 2026-05-25 to meet their board review.

Attachments: pricing-summary-FintechCo-20260518.xlsx, MOU-FintechCo-draft.pdf

Ask: Can we get an initial executive greenlight on the commercial structure (price lock + uplift cap + renewal protection)? If approved, legal will draft explicit contract language.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 36-month rate commitment & renewal protection (FintechCo)

Lauren —

I reviewed the numbers. Commercially this is a strategic account: retention risk low, potential expansion into data services later. I support the idea of a 36-month price commitment with an annual uplift cap — that will make procurement comfortable and should accelerate sign. That said, two flags:

1) The 20% onboarding discount pushes implied ARR reduction close to our reserved capacity threshold for Dedicated SKU; we need finance confirmation on unit economics.
2) Renewal protection language as stated could create a perpetual protection that prevents any meaningful price parity adjustments if we need to reprice based on hardware cost changes. Legal will want precise boundaries (e.g., cap applies only to list-price increases up to X%).

Recommend: escalate to execs for approval on principle (36 months at locked rate + 5% uplift cap + 20% first-year discount) with a requirement that Legal and Finance provide binding language and revenue recognition plan before signature.

Nikhil
Head of Sales Operations

Team —

I am prepared to provide a conditional executive approval to move this forward to Legal and Finance, with the following constraints:

- Approve up to 28% onboarding discount year 1 (not 20% stacked on other concessions) — this aligns with our discount bands for strategic anchors.
- Approve 36-month rate commitment (price lock) subject to a documented annual uplift cap of 5% absolute (no compounding ambiguity).
- Renewal protection: approve a clause that guarantees customers receive written notice 12 months before any list-price change >5% and a one-time credit equal to the delta for the first renewal period. Legal to define precise credit mechanics; no perpetual floor beyond the 36-month term unless both parties agree.
- Include a performance-based clawback: if utilization is <50% of committed minimum in year 2, apply a 2% credit to year 3 billing (protects units economics).

This is conditional on clear language from Legal and a revenue recognition memo from Finance (Marissa) that outlines any deferral impact. If Finance signs off, I will provide final sign-off by EOD 2026-05-21.

Rishi

Team —

Thanks for the heads up. Finance has reviewed the sketch. High-level notes:

- Revenue recognition: a 36-month price lock with a material upfront discount will require us to spread the discount across the committed term if we treat the onboarding incentive as a contract concession. We need Legal to call out whether the onboarding discount is a one-time credit (delivery of a separate service) or an adjustment to the committed consideration. This decision materially affects ARR reporting in year 1 vs. year 2/3.

- Clawback/credits: the proposed 2% performance credit is acceptable but must be capped overall (e.g., cumulative credits cannot exceed 5% of total committed value). Otherwise, it's a margin leak. Please add that cap to the term sheet.

- Suggested commercial tweak to protect margins while keeping procurement happy: keep the 36-month rate commitment but add a minimum annual billing floor equal to 70% of committed ARR. If consumption falls below that, billing remains at the floor until catch-up. This gives FintechCo predictability while protecting Redwood.

If Legal confirms we can model the onboarding discount as a separate one-time credit (not amortized), Finance can sign off. Otherwise, I need 24 hours after Legal's language to recalc deferrals.

Marissa
Head of Finance — Enterprise Deals

Subject: Exec approval: FintechCo 36-month commitment

Team —

Having reviewed the thread and Finance's feedback, I approve the following, effective for FintechCo (RWI-3749):

- Approve 36-month rate commitment at the proposed locked rate.
- Approve annual uplift cap of 5% (absolute).
- Approve onboarding discount up to 20% for year 1, provided Legal's language treats it as a one-time credit to avoid amortization; otherwise cap discount at 15%.
- Approve renewal protection wording as Rishi described (12-month notice + one-time credit at renewal if list-price change >5%), with Legal to produce final language; no perpetual price floor beyond the three-year term without mutual agreement.
- Require insertion of minimum annual billing floor at 70% of committed ARR and a cumulative cap on credits of 5% of committed value.

Lauren — please proceed to finalize legal language and send the DocuSign packet to FintechCo once Legal confirms the credit/amortization treatment. Marissa, loop back with updated revenue schedule when Legal shares the draft.

Signed,
